chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who guaranteed the debt of another man, then settled (compounded) the debt with him. He said: 'He is entitled only to what he settled with him.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.صَالَحَ: settled / compounded (reached an agreement to settle a debt)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a guarantor who settles a debtor's debt?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that a guarantor's right of recourse (*raji'*) is confined strictly to the specific terms of the settlement (*sulh*) they negotiated, rather than automatically reverting to the original debt principal. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that *sulh* creates a new contractual obligation, thereby modifying the guarantor's claim against the debtor to reflect the actual consideration paid or agreed upon. It underscores the importance of precise contractual intent in commercial transactions within Islamic law.
